title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority-aware burst controls and utilization reporting enhancement
author: Sofia Ramirez
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler to support priority-aware burst controls and improves utilization reporting for fleet dashboards. Includes new metrics and a backlog of test/QA steps.
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while allowing high-priority traffic to burst temporarily without starving best-effort tenants. Previous autoscaler and token-bucket smoothing behaved uniformly across priorities which caused suboptimal tail latency during mixed-priority spikes. This change introduces priority-aware burst controls and richer utilization reporting to help operators tune policies.

What this PR does: - Introduces a priority token bucket layer in the fleet autoscaler that tracks per-priority burst budgets and enforces configurable smoothing and recharge rates. - Adds a priority routing hint to the autoscaler API so schedulers can prefer nodes with available priority budget. - Improves utilization reporting: per-pool and per-priority utilization metrics, 1m/5m/1h percentiles, and burst budget time-series. - Exposes new dashboards and alerting rules (SLO: burst budget exhaustion rate, SLA: 99p latency for high priority). - Adds integration tests and a focused perf canary to validate behavior under mixed workloads.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1421) - [x] Unit tests for token bucket logic - [x] Integration tests for scheduler interaction - [x] Perf canary added to perf-lab - [x] Dashboard panels + queries added to observability-pack - [x] Backwards compatible config schema (existing autoscaler config still valid)

Motivation: We observed during customer canaries that high-priority traffic (dedicated SLA routes) could suffer due to large bursts from lower-priority tenants. By making burst budgets priority-aware and surfacing budget exhaustion in dashboards, operators can set recharge rates and per-priority throughput guarantees that align with customer SLAs.

Risk and mitigations: The risk is misconfiguration leading to underutilized fleets. Mitigations: default recharge and burst limits are conservative; feature gated behind a config flag in Dedicated; rollout via canary and staged rollout to fleets.

Related: previous PRs that iterated on burst reporting and smoothing: pr-21437, pr-1023456, pr-1428790 (see repo history). Linked Linear ticket ENG-1421 contains design and expected observability queries.

Notes for reviewer: Focus on the tokenbucket math (autoscaler/burst/token_bucket.go), API changes to the autoscaler control plane (autoscaler/api/v1/config.proto), and the new observability metrics (observability/metrics/burst_budget_metrics.prom). The scheduler integration is intentionally lightweight: scheduler checks budget availability before assigning high-priority tasks.

b4d5e6f: add API flag and config schema changes
c7d8e9a: wire priority hint into scheduler assignment path
d0e1f2a: add metrics and dashboard queries for per-priority utilization
e3f4a5b: integration tests + perf canary config
review_comments: Ava Chen: overall looks good. Please add a unit test for the edge case where recharge_rate=0.
Sofia Ramirez: added test; also tightened validation on config parsing to reject negative rates.
Liam Patel: can you confirm the default values won't change current fleet behavior? I suggest a small doc blurb for operators.
Sofia Ramirez: defaults preserved; added release notes and a short operator guide in docs/design.
Noah Gonzales: approved after reading perf canary results showing no regression in average utilization and improved 99p for high-priority routes.
notes: Staged rollout: enabled by default on non-production fleets; enterprise customers can toggle via Dedicated console. Observability queries and dashboard JSON included for immediate deployment.
performance_summary: Perf canary against fleet size 50 with mixed 70/30 low/high priority traffic: - High-priority 99p latency improved from 420ms to 210ms under burst events - Overall CPU utilization stable (+1.2% average) - Burst budget exhaustion events reduced by ~78%
backwards_compatibility: Config schema change is additive; existing fields unchanged. Feature gated behind 'enable_priority_burst' flag in autoscaler config.
testing_notes: Ran full CI and two manual canaries. Integration test simulates sustained low-priority burst and asserts high-priority tail latency and that recharge_rate limits are honored.
operator_actions: After deploy: 1) Monitor dashboard 'Dedicated / Burst Budget / Priority' 2) Tune recharge_rate for low-priority pools if utilization drops 3) If burst budgets consistently exhaust, consider raising committed capacity or adjusting per-route throughput guarantees
changelog_entry: Added priority-aware burst budgets and improved utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets. Defaults preserve prior behavior; opt-in via config flag for early testing.
